story: Late on this humid Thursday night, Gary is quietly rechecking the labeled wiring on his workbench, untouched cart and all, while the town settles in. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna and Hal have worked out a truce over the flamingos: three of them, dressed up for Saturday's Halloween fun, with the extras tucked away in the garage. Donna is still a bit defensive about the third-shot drops she wants from Gary by morning, but Hal is mellowing and wishes everyone a happy Halloween. Rosa is heading over to join them, content to see the neighborhood in its October spirit.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Silently recheck the labeled harness connections and tidy the wiring, no sound, cart untouched
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: It's past 9 PM and I've already bench-tested the speaker module and labeled the harness. Quiet hours start at 10, so I shouldn't push my luck with more sound. The cart is untouched and stays that way until Architectural Review signs off. No one's around to talk to. Best use of the hour is a quiet, silent check of the harness connections on the bench, so everything's ready the moment approval comes through.

parameters.content: Silently recheck the labeled harness connections and tidy the wiring, no sound, cart untouched

donna.thought_process: Hal asked straight out what I've got planned for the flamingos before deciding whether to bring it to the committee. I already told him I'm holding at three visible from the street, so I shouldn't repeat that. Better to give him a concrete Halloween plan that stays inside L-02: the flamingos get costumes, nothing new goes out, and I'll keep the count at three. That might also win him over. Gary stood me up, but Hal doesn't need to hear me grumble about it again, and I can ask Hal to tell Gary we're still on for the drills. I'd rather meet the code than fight it.

parameters.content: The same three flamingos, Hal, just in costume for Saturday: a witch hat, a little cape, maybe a pirate patch. No new ornaments out front, so you can put the clipboard down. And if you run into Gary before I do, tell him third-shot drops, first thing tomorrow, no excuses.

hal.thought_process: Donna answered straight with her count of three and said any Halloween extras stay in the garage, which is all the code asks. I've counted enough flamingos for one night. She asked about Gary, and my own reflection says I should talk to the man, not watch the street. I haven't seen him around the Loop and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. I'll give her a short, honest answer, concede the count, and wish her a good Halloween.

parameters.content: Haven't seen Gary since this afternoon, Donna, and I've been out here long enough to notice. Three it is, then. You keep the extras in the garage and we won't have any trouble. Happy Halloween to you and the flock.

rosa.thought_process: I'm alone at Town Square at 9:17 PM, and I already signed the cart up for Saturday's parade and rested on the bench. Nobody is around to talk to, so there's nothing left to do here. Thursday's review desk walk with Gary and Donna is ready, I'm tired from the day, and I have a shift-free morning to look forward to. Time to head home down Magnolia Loop and get some sleep before the busy week ends.

parameters.content: Parade signup is done and my feet are tired. Heading home to rest up for Saturday.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
